corrective_scope: Executes the Consolidated Final Corrective document (which replaces and cancels the previously issued Sixth Corrective), responding to findings F1-F6 of the independent audit against the Batch 10.4 Fifth Corrective. No Batch 10.5 work performed. No UI, clipboard, download, backup, restore, Prompt Pack, rendered-image, persistence-write, or external-integration work performed.

findings_addressed.F1: A fully bijective exchange of two real Output A ids between two in-scope pair-bearing identities - previously a documented, unclosed limitation - is now rejected. hasNumberingCanonicalOrderViolation requires plan.numbering's outputAId sequence to equal plan.scope.outputAIds exactly (length, value, index, never sorted or deduplicated); a bijective swap changes the sequence at each swapped identity's position relative to the untouched scope array, which the exact-sequence comparison catches without any schema change or re-derivation from the source project.
findings_addressed.F2: Extra hostile numbering rows are now rejected and never reach README/manifest/ZIP content. The same canonical-sequence check closes this: an injected row (first, middle, or last) changes plan.numbering.length relative to plan.scope.outputAIds.length, failing the exact-length-and-value comparison before any content is built.
findings_addressed.F3: scope.sceneIds duplicate/inconsistency handling is now composite rather than a blanket exclusion. Single-session scopes still require sceneIds to have no duplicate; complete_project/all scopes now require selection.sessions to equal scope.sessionIds exactly (order and value) and the flattened per-session scene lists (in that order) to equal scope.sceneIds exactly - so a scene id legitimately reused once per distinct session still passes, while an isolated scope.sceneIds override inconsistent with the real per-session data, or an extra unaccounted occurrence, now fails.
findings_addressed.F4: Fixed the real production bug in src/engines/export-engine/selection.ts: Output A/B/execution-plan selection built its numbering lookup from a scene-only Map (new Map(numbering.map(entry => [entry.sceneId, entry]))). Since a SceneId is only unique within its own session, two sessions reusing the same scene id silently collided in that flat map, and the later session's numbering row overwrote the earlier session's - misattributing scene numbers and A/B labels across sessions in exactly the reproduction the audit gave (session 1's own scene inheriting session 2's '2A'/'2B' labels). Replaced with a nested (sessionId -> sceneId -> entry) map; verified against the exact §12.1 mandatory fixture (session-1/scene-shared=1, session-2/scene-extra=1, session-2/scene-shared=2) producing the required 1A/1B, 1A/1B, 2A/2B numbering and package paths.
findings_addressed.F5: Added a genuine, committed same-sceneId-different-ordinal test (Consolidated Final Corrective §12.1) reproducing the exact adversarial construction from the audit, plus a numbering matrix (extra/missing/duplicate/out-of-scope/fake-id/permutation/label/scene-number cases) and a group-numbering matrix (duplicate/extra/missing/mismatch/wrong-label/out-of-group-scene cases) that did not exist before this corrective.
findings_addressed.F6: Delivers a committed, reproducible external ZIP verification command (npm run verify:zip:external, backed by scripts/verify-golden-zips-external.mjs and test/export-engine/packaging/golden-zip-dump.test.ts) rather than relying on ad hoc scratch scripts as the only evidence - it builds all 10 golden fixtures plus one deliberately physically-reordered-but-Info-ZIP-tolerated archive from the current code, independently verifies every fixture via the system unzip binary, and confirms the reordered archive is externally accepted while verifyPackageZip rejects it with the exact structural/local_order_mismatch reason.

architecture_note: hasScopePolicyViolation, hasDuplicateScopeIdentifiers, hasNumberingCanonicalOrderViolation, hasNumberingFieldViolation, hasGroupNumberingViolation, and hasRelationalIntegrityViolation are each still their own narrow, unit-testable function, but package.ts now calls exactly one entry point - validatePackagePlanIntegrity - in one fixed precedence order, replacing what had grown into a sequence of independently-invoked boolean checks.
